facts.text: The Brush Cuckoo is a grey-brown bird with a buff breast and a call that is a familiar sound of the Australian bush.
facts.quote: It is a grey-brown bird with a buff breast. Its call is a familiar sound of the Australian and Indonesian bush.

facts.text: Its wings are sharply pointed and backswept in flight.
facts.quote: The wings are sharply pointed and backswept in flight.

facts.text: It is a brood parasite whose females lay different egg types matched to different host species.
facts.quote: The Sahul brush cuckoo is a brood parasite. Its eggs are polymorphic, meaning females lay specific egg types for specific hosts.

facts.text: Across its Australian range it exploits at least 58 other bird species as hosts.
facts.quote: Across its Australian range the Sahul brush cuckoo exploits at least 58 other avian species

facts.text: Australian hosts that raise its chicks include the purple-crowned fairywren and several honeyeaters, flycatchers and fantails.
facts.quote: they include the purple-crowned fairywren, brown-backed honeyeater, bar-breasted honeyeater and for C. v. variolosus they include the rose robin, Norfolk robin, leaden flycatcher, restless flycatcher, satin flycatcher, rufous fantail and grey fantail.

facts.text: In Australia it lives in rainforests, rainforest edges, mangrove forests, secondary forests and plantations.
facts.quote: it is known to inhabit a range of environments including rainforests, rainforest edges, mangrove forests, secondary forests, and plantations.

facts.text: The Brush Cuckoo ranges from northern and eastern Australia to New Guinea, the Solomon Islands and Malaysia.
facts.quote: It is native to Malesia, New Guinea, the Solomon Islands and northern and eastern Australia.

facts.text: It is migratory in the southern part of its Australian range.
facts.quote: In Australia, it is migratory in the southern part of its range.
